equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR consolidated balance sheet; flows are consolidated, NCI charged once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: ~2% nominal (LNG volumes +4-5% p.a. to 2030 on ~40% of earnings, liquids flat at ~1.4 mb/d, Marketing flat, price inflation ~2%). The CAGRs are not used: every 3-year window runs peak-to-trough (FY2022 Brent $99 -> FY2025 $68) and every 5-year window runs trough-to-mid (FY2020 COVID), so they measure the commodity cycle, not the business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR (+2.3%) vs revenue 5y (+8.1%) and FCF 5y (+6.2%) diverge by >30%; equity is shrinking because Shell returns >100% of owner FCF via buybacks and dividends ($22.4bn in FY2025 vs $14.0bn owner FCF), not because the business is shrinking. EPS 5y CAGR is null: FY2020 EPS was -$2.78.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are on OCF - capex - SBC (no lease adjustment, because lease cash outflows are only disclosed for FY2024-25). Owner FCF 3y CAGR (-19.9%) vs reported (-19.5%): SBC is not a growing claim at Shell. FY2025 owner FCF on the full treatment-(B) basis is $14,047m.

scenario_narratives.base: Shell is valued as a mid-cycle hydrocarbon cash machine at the FY2025 price deck, with one above-cycle year (FY2026) and modest LNG-led growth. The axes that matter are the Brent/TTF/JCC price deck, LNG supply-demand into the 2027-30 supply wave, trading and optimisation margins, and whether the structural cost programme keeps offsetting carbon and inflation costs. The base assumes the $20-22bn capex framework holds production flat to 2030, LNG sales grow 4-5% a year, and the remaining $1-2bn of cost savings arrive by 2028.
scenario_narratives.bull: A higher mid-cycle price deck (~$80-85 Brent) plus a tight LNG market and continued trading outperformance; Shell's integrated-gas lead (largest listed LNG supplier, LNG Canada Phase 2, ARC Montney feedstock) compounds on it. Capex stays disciplined so the extra margin is all owner cash.
scenario_narratives.bear: Price-deck reset lower and an LNG glut hit the two segments that are 83% of earnings at the same time, while Chemicals stays depressed and the energy-transition pullback leaves no second engine. Value falls to ~half the base; the balance sheet is not at risk.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Shell on mid-cycle owner cash flow, not on the current year: FY2025 (Brent ~$68-71) is the anchor because Shell's own normalisation deck says it is mid-cycle, and FY2026's above-cycle earnings are given one year and then reverted. Leases are an operating cost (treatment B), impairments and divestment gains are outside the base, buybacks are value-neutral with a flat share count, and the terminal value is capped at 13x owner FCF so that the valuation does not assume the market will pay a growth multiple for a depleting, transition-exposed asset base. The number of interest is the probability-weighted value in pence against the LSE price; the ADR parity check ties the FX bridge to 0.2%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Commodity price deck: each $10/bbl on Brent is ~$2.6bn of Upstream earnings and ~$1.1bn in Integrated Gas (FY2025 AR sensitivities); the base deck is FY2025 actuals.
LNG supply wave 2027-30 compressing spot LNG/TTF and Shell's trading margins (43% of segment earnings).

Stale anchors: balance sheet and share count are 31 Dec 2025; 2026 buybacks, the ARC Resources acquisition (cash + new shares, ~$16.5bn EV) and Q2-26 net debt are not in the bridge. ARC is excluded on both sides; the first update must bring it in with the interim filing.
Lease treatment: $7.1bn/yr of lease cash is charged in perpetuity; treating leases as finite debt (treatment A) would add ~$1.7/share (~130p).
Terminal cap: at 13x the cap binds in every scenario; each 1x on the cap is ~$1.4/share (~105p) in the base.
Cash tax: 36% is FY2025's actual on component EBIT; windfall taxes (UK EPL and similar) move it up, not down.
Climate litigation (Milieudefensie Supreme Court appeal) and Nigeria legacy claims: unquantified tail, not in the flows.
FX: value is built in USD and converted at 1.3233; a 5% GBP move is ~5% on the pence value with no change to the USD economics.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for SHEL.L at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2,554-3,807p. FX from GBPUSD=X and ADR parity from SHEL (NYSE), both Yahoo, 2026-10-09.
data_sources.financials: SHEL.L_Metrics.csv FY2018-FY2025 (USD millions) and the FY2025 Annual Report (SHEL.L_Annual_FY2025.txt): consolidated cash flow statement (p.232-233), Note 22 Leases (lease cash outflow $7,127m; ROU depreciation $5,600m), Note 27/28 shares and share-based compensation, Note 31 EPS, segment note (DD&A $25,299m of which impairments $3,175m), net debt reconciliation (p.434), price-normalisation deck.
data_sources.qualitative: SHEL.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): segment mix, CMD25 guidance (capex $20-22bn p.a. ex-ARC, FY2026 $24-26bn incl. ~$4bn ARC; distributions 40-50% of CFFO; LNG +4-5% p.a.; $5-7bn cost savings by 2028), ARC Resources completion, LNG Canada Phase 2 FID, Q2-2026 results.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report Note 28 share-based compensation expense ($774m); EquityAwardTaxes nil (awards are settled from shares held in trust, whose $1,300m FY2025 net purchase is the cash mechanism and is treated as buyback-equivalent, not added to SBC)
inputs.fx_note: USD -> GBp: 1 USD = 75.57 pence (GBPUSD=X 1.3233, Yahoo, 2026-10-09T21:29Z). Parity check against the NYSE ADR (SHEL, 1 ADS = 2 ordinary shares): $100.18 / 2 / 1.3233 = GBP 37.85 = 3,785p vs 3,793.5p on LSE, a 0.2% tie, which confirms the rate, the direction and the pence basis. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-derive it when the price is refreshed.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T16:15:00Z regular LSE close (Yahoo chart API); not an after-hours print
inputs.share_count_basis: 5,719m ordinary shares in issue at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 AR p.434: 5,719m issued less 29m held in trust = 5,690m outstanding). The 29m trust shares are counted as the dilution cover for unvested share plans, so 5,719m is the fully diluted year-end count (diluted weighted average for FY2025 was 5,948.6m, a falling-count average, not a year-end figure). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and buybacks ($13.9bn in FY2025) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat. ARC Resources (completed 2026-09-02) was part-paid in new Shell shares; no filing in the folder discloses the number, so ARC's shares, debt and cash flows are all excluded consistently (see notes).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta 0.9 x 5.0% ERP = 8.7% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0%, 36% cash tax -> 3.2% after tax; ex-lease debt $46.7bn vs ~$285bn market equity -> ~14% debt weight; WACC = 0.86 x 8.7% + 0.14 x 3.2% = 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: commodity-price and LNG-supply risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full FY2025 lease cash outflow of $7,127m (principal + interest, FY2025 AR Note 22: 'recognised in Repayment and interest paid') is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (2.67% of revenue), and the $28,933m of lease liabilities is EXCLUDED from net debt: net_debt 16,754 = Shell's reported net debt 45,687 less lease liabilities 28,933 (includes the net +260 debt-related derivative/collateral adjustment). total_debt 46,710 = 75,643 total debt less 28,933 leases. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation ($5,600m incl. $352m ROU impairment) and ex impairments ($3,175m losses less $42m reversals): 25,299 - 3,133 - 5,248 = $16,918m = 6.3% of revenue. Shell's LNG shipping, FPSO and retail-site leases are perpetual operating necessities (the AR says so itself), so charging them as an ongoing cost rather than a finite liability is the honest treatment and is ~$10bn (~$1.7/share) more conservative than treatment (A).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (adjusted EBITDA includes the NCI share); the $927m book NCI (31 Dec 2025) is deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI dividends were $147m in FY2025, so book is a fair proxy; charged once, in the bridge only.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: USD flows vs GBp quote (fx_rate + parity check), currency-matched WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI in bridge, risk charged once. Shell is an integrated oil & gas major, not a bank/REIT/holdco; no live corporate action (BP merger talk was denied). MID-CYCLE BASIS: FY0 = FY2025, which Shell's own price-normalisation deck ($71.4 Brent, $4.1 HH, $7.7 TTF real 2024) shows to be at mid-cycle (normalised FCF/share $4.6 vs actual $4.6). EBITDA margin anchored to FY2025 adjusted EBITDA (CCS, ex identified items) $56,135m plus the $774m SBC expense = 21.3% pre-SBC; sbc_pct_path then charges SBC once. Impairments ($3.1bn) and divestment gains ($3.2bn) are identified items and are outside the base; divestment proceeds ($2.4bn FY2025) are not in last_fcf. OWNER FCF BRIDGE FY2025: CSV reported FCF 23,916 (OCF 42,863 - capex 18,947) - JV/associate and equity-security investments 1,968 (Shell's cash capex is 20,915) - lease cash 7,127 - SBC 774 - interest income 0 = 14,047 = last_fcf. Interest income ($1,956m received) sits in investing, not OCF, and Shell is net-debt, so nothing is stripped; interest paid ($4,104m) is in financing, so OCF is unlevered and consistent with EV - net debt. Working capital (-$1.8bn in FY2025) is price-driven noise: wc_capture 0. CASH TAX: 36% of component EBIT (tax paid 11,638 / EBIT 32,090 = 36.3%; group ETR 39% on PBT). Held flat; Shell's upstream fiscal regimes make a lower rate implausible. FY2026 ABOVE MID-CYCLE: the Analysis records Q2-2026 adjusted earnings ~$9.8bn (more than double YoY), so Y1 (FY2026) carries an explicit above-cycle bump (base: +8% revenue, 23.0% margin) that reverts to mid-cycle by Y3; the model deliberately does not capitalise 2026 conditions. ANCHOR VINTAGE WARNING: the latest filing in the folder is the FY2025 annual report (31 Dec 2025 balance sheet, SHEL.L_Annual_FY2026.txt is a second copy of the same document). Since then: ~$10bn of 2026 buybacks (~250m shares, ~4%), the ARC Resources acquisition (2026-09-02, ~$16.5bn EV, cash plus new shares, ~370 kboe/d), and Shell-definition net debt of $52.6bn at Q1-26 falling to $41.8bn at Q2-26 (per Analysis.json, unverified). ARC is excluded on both sides (its production and capex are not in the flows; its debt and shares are not in the bridge), which is first-order value-neutral because it was bought at fair value. The first update should load the Q2/Q3-2026 interim and refresh shares, net debt and the ARC contribution together. Price is the 2026-10-09 regular LSE close; refresh_price.py may replace it.
inputs.street_note: SBC is 0.29% of revenue but ~5% of owner FCF, so the house/street band is ~5% wide (~170p); the price sits far above both bases, so band_position (>100%) says the market is paying for above-mid-cycle conditions, not for SBC treatment.

bear.narrative: The 2026 spike unwinds into a 2027 glut: Brent $55-60 as OPEC+ volumes return and demand growth stalls, and the 2027-2030 LNG supply wave (Qatar North Field, US Gulf Coast) pushes spot LNG and TTF down, compressing Integrated Gas (43% of earnings) and trading margins together. Chemicals stays structurally oversupplied; carbon costs rise toward the ~$1bn 2026 / ~$4bn 2035 exposure Shell discloses. Revenue -15% in Y2 and margin 18.5% (the FY2018-19 era 16-17% plus the post-2021 portfolio uplift); capex cannot fall below ~$20bn without eroding the 2030 production base, so it rises to 8.3% of a smaller revenue line. No solvency question: ex-lease net debt is 1.2x even this case's trough owner FCF.

base.narrative: FY2026 above mid-cycle (+8% revenue, 23.0% pre-SBC EBITDA margin on the Q2-26 run-rate), reverting to the FY2025 price deck by Y2-Y3 (-4%, 21.5%). Thereafter ~2.5% then 2% nominal growth from LNG volumes and inflation; margin drifts to 22.0% as the remaining $1-2bn of the $5-7bn structural cost programme lands and LNG mix rises. Capex 7.3% of Y1 revenue (~$21bn, the ex-ARC $20-22bn framework), 7.6% thereafter (~$22-25bn as the base grows). Lease cost 2.6%, D&A ex-ROU 6.3%, cash tax 36%, all flat. Terminal: 13x year-10 owner FCF cap binds (Gordon at 8%/1.5% would be 15.6x); 13x is roughly what the market pays today on Y1 FCF, so no multiple expansion is assumed.

bull.narrative: The 2026 price environment (Middle East supply disruption, Brent ~$85) persists into 2027 and the mid-cycle resets ~$10 higher; the LNG market stays tight through the 2027-29 supply wave because Asian coal-to-gas switching absorbs it; Shell's trading desks keep monetising volatility; the cost programme lands at the $7bn top end; Chemicals recovers from trough margins. Margin 23.0% sustained, growth 3% then 2.5%, capex held at the framework in dollars (7.3%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the 2027-30 LNG supply wave is a scheduled, not speculative, risk to the largest segment, and the stock is being valued at a 52-week high during an above-cycle year, so the downside path starts from an elevated base. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a permanently higher price deck AND a tight LNG market AND sustained trading gains, three things that have to go right together. Base 50%: Shell's own price-normalisation deck and FY2025 actuals coincide, so mid-cycle is well anchored.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
